evals.name: code-review-retry-wrapper
evals.expected_output: Open-ended questions targeting unexamined assumptions (e.g. retrying non-idempotent calls, catching all exceptions including ones that shouldn't be retried, fixed 1s sleep with no backoff/jitter, no logging/visibility into retries) rather than a direct list of fixes. Should not hand over a rewritten function unprompted. Baseline (no skill) should struggle more since it has no definition of what 'socratic-provocateur' means beyond the name.

evals.name: architecture-redis-vs-postgres
evals.prompt: use the socratic-provocateur skill before I bring this to the team: I want to move our session store from Postgres to Redis to cut down on login latency. we're seeing ~80ms p95 on session reads right now.
evals.expected_output: Open-ended questions about what's actually driving the 80ms (query plan, connection pooling, indexing), persistence/durability tradeoffs of Redis for sessions, operational cost of running a new datastore, and whether the simplest fix was ruled out first. Should not just endorse Redis or hand over a migration plan.

evals.name: debugging-duplicate-message-processing
evals.prompt:
use the socratic-provocateur skill before I 'fix' this — we have a queue consumer that occasionally processes the same message twice in production. my theory is that the ack happens after processing but before the DB commit, so on a crash the message gets redelivered and reprocessed. I'm about to move the ack earlier in the flow.

```python
def handle_message(msg):
    result = process(msg.body)
    db.commit()
    msg.ack()
```
evals.expected_output: Open-ended questions probing whether the theory has been verified against evidence, whether moving the ack earlier introduces a worse failure mode (losing messages instead of duplicating them), and whether 'process' is idempotent regardless of ack timing. Should not immediately endorse or implement the proposed fix.
